core.title: A machine learning enhanced substructure method for full scale topology optimization of piezoelectric graded lattice structure
core.abstract: Owing to their ultra-light weight, high compliance, and superior fracture resistance, piezoelectric graded lattice structures hold significant engineering potential for electromechanical devices. However, the three-dimensional (3D) full-scale topology optimization of such structures is severely hindered by the prohibitive computational costs of electromechanical coupling analysis. To address the issue, this paper proposes a machine learning (ML)-accelerated scheme for the large-scale explicit topology optimization of piezoelectric graded lattice structures. By integrating the 3D moving morphable components (MMC) approach with the partitioned coordinate mapping (PCM), this scheme achieves precise geometric construction of lattice skeletons. To overcome the computational bottleneck, a ML-accelerated scheme for the prediction of numerical shape function is developed, complemented by a physical residual-driven online correction strategy to tackle the degradation of the generalization at discontinuous 0/1 topological boundaries. Numerical validations demonstrate that the scheme drastically enhances computational efficiency while preserving global finite element analysis accuracy. Notably, computation time for a one-million degree-of-freedom (DOF) structure is reduced from 981.01 to 6.91 s. The developed approach is validated through three 3D full-scale numerical examples, including a cantilever beam, a cantilever plate, and an enclosed cylindrical energy harvester. Optimization results demonstrate that this scheme for electromechanical coupling problems is highly efficient and robust, effectively driving topology reconstruction to suppress local charge cancellation effects. Consequently, the final energy conversion rate is enhanced by up to 1.56 times over the initial configuration. Furthermore, comparisons confirm that these lattice structures yield higher absolute electrical energy output than conventional dense solid designs, which highlights their anticipated values in the applications in environmental energy harvesting.

core.title: The AI-FinTech Entrepreneurial Ecosystem: Exploring How Intelligent Financial Technologies and Algorithmic Digital Visibility Transform Opportunity Recognition and Venture Growth. A Comparative Study of Pakistan and China
core.venue: Journal of Business Insight and Innovation
core.abstract: Artificial intelligence and financial technology are increasingly intertwined with the digital platforms through which entrepreneurs discover opportunities, secure finance, reach customers, and scale ventures. This qualitative comparative study develops an integrated view of the AI-FinTech entrepreneurial ecosystem by examining how intelligent financial technologies and algorithmic digital visibility shape opportunity recognition and venture growth in Pakistan and China. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with 20 entrepreneurs, equally divided between the two countries, and the data were analyzed using reflexive thematic analysis. The analysis identifies six interrelated themes: AI-FinTech as an opportunity-sensing infrastructure; algorithmic visibility as a market-access mechanism; intelligent finance as a resource-orchestration capability; platform opacity and dependency; ecosystem asymmetry between Pakistan and China; and human judgment, trust, and governance as boundary conditions. The comparative findings indicate that AI-enabled financial intelligence creates value most effectively when entrepreneurs can convert data into action and when digital platforms provide stable routes to visibility, legitimacy, and customers. The study contributes an ecosystem-level explanation linking entrepreneurial alertness, dynamic capabilities, digital finance, and algorithmic visibility. core.title: A Hybrid Large Language Model and Diffusion Framework for Rational Promoter Design
core.abstract: High-performance promoters are essential tools for precisely regulating gene expression, yet their rational design within the vast combinatorial sequence space remains a major challenge. Here, we present a hybrid framework that integrates a large language model (LLM) with a diffusion model to enable data-driven and interpretable promoter design. The fine-tuned LLM predicts promoter strength with high accuracy and, through systematic sequence mutations, identifies biologically essential core regions. A diffusion model is then conditioned on these core regions to reconstruct non-core regions and generate complete promoter sequences. We experimentally validated this approach in Escherichia coli by high-throughput barcoded promoter activity sequencing: 7.78% of the designed promoters outperformed the benchmark promoter BBa_J23119, with the best variants reaching approximately 2.5-fold the expression level of BBa_J23119. By explicitly coupling interpretability with generative design, this strategy provides a practical framework for promoter design in E. coli and may be adaptable to other regulatory sequence engineering tasks.

core.title: Risk-Aware Predictive Maintenance for Aero-Engines via CVaR-Guided Reinforcement Learning and LLM-Based Risk Abstraction
core.abstract: A fundamental limitation of current predictive maintenance is the inability to transform prognostic uncertainty into actionable decisions, which often leads to either wasteful early interventions or catastrophic failures in aero-engines. To address this, we propose the Risk-Aware Predictive Maintenance (RAPM) framework consisting of four integrated components: a probabilistic stacked sparse autoencoder that extracts degradation features while providing distributional remaining useful life (RUL) predictions; a Monte Carlo Dropout module with Conditional Value at Risk (CVaR) that summarizes lower-tail predictive risk and produces a conservative RUL estimate for decision making; a locally deployed large language model (Qwen2.5-3B) that abstracts numerical uncertainty into discrete semantic risk levels, enabling interpretable reward shaping; and a Proximal Policy Optimization agent trained with curriculum learning to handle long-horizon sparse-reward maintenance optimization. On the NASA C-MAPSS FD001 benchmark, RAPM achieves a 96.0% optimal stopping rate with no late interventions or failure events compared with 90.2% for the strongest independent maintenance baseline. Under controlled substitution with LSTM-MCD, Transformer-MCD, CNN-MCD, and Deep Ensemble prognostic backbones, the same CVaR-LLM-PPO decision architecture maintains optimal stopping rates of 92.4–95.2% with no late interventions or failure events. Within the matched Rule-PPO ablation, CVaR increases the mean optimal stopping rate from 92.0% to 95.0% under unperturbed conditions, which is a gain of 3.0 percentage points. Under Gaussian sensor noise (σ=0.05), the gain reaches 9.0 percentage points, from 73.0% to 82.0%. These results demonstrate that the decision benefit of RAPM extends across independently trained prognostic models.

core.title: Large Language Model-Driven Predictive Maintenance for Complex Industrial Processes: A Review and Future Research Directions
core.abstract: With the rapid advancement of industrial intelligence, equipment predictive maintenance (PdM) has emerged as a critical enabler for intelligent operation and maintenance (O&M) systems. However, conventional machine learning-based PdM methods are inherently constrained by scarce labeled fault samples, weak cross-condition generalization, and a lack of advanced causal reasoning capabilities in complex industrial process environments. Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) and generative artificial intelligence (GAI) have created unprecedented opportunities to fundamentally overcome these persistent PdM limitations. This paper presents a comprehensive review and future perspective on LLM applications for PdM in industrial process systems and proposes a hierarchical “Capability-Domain-Method (CDM)” taxonomy to establish a unified analytical framework for this fast-growing research field. Based on a systematic analysis of the 103 core research papers published between 2016 and 2026, this work comprehensively summarizes the latest research on LLMs for predictive maintenance from three core technical dimensions: data augmentation, model adaptation, and knowledge reasoning and decision-making. Data augmentation methods generate high-fidelity fault samples and degradation patterns to mitigate industrial data scarcity and class imbalance. Model adaptation techniques empower general-purpose pre-trained LLMs to adapt to specific equipment and complex industrial environments. Knowledge reasoning and decision-making approaches integrate external industrial domain knowledge, autonomous reasoning mechanisms, and maintenance decision processes to improve the performance of fault diagnosis, root cause analysis, and maintenance decision-making. Furthermore, this paper discusses key challenges related to operational reliability, deep domain adaptation, unified evaluation standards, and unified deployment efficiency. Finally, future research directions are advised, including physics-informed large models, industrial domain-specific models, autonomous maintenance agents, and standardized open benchmarking platforms, to accelerate the paradigm shift in PdM from data-driven pattern to knowledge-driven and autonomous decision-making.

papers.title: A machine learning enhanced substructure method for full scale topology optimization of piezoelectric graded lattice structure
papers.abstract: Owing to their ultra-light weight, high compliance, and superior fracture resistance, piezoelectric graded lattice structures hold significant engineering potential for electromechanical devices. However, the three-dimensional (3D) full-scale topology optimization of such structures is severely hindered by the prohibitive computational costs of electromechanical coupling analysis. To address the issue, this paper proposes a machine learning (ML)-accelerated scheme for the large-scale explicit topology optimization of piezoelectric graded lattice structures. By integrating the 3D moving morphable components (MMC) approach with the partitioned coordinate mapping (PCM), this scheme achieves precise geometric construction of lattice skeletons. To overcome the computational bottleneck, a ML-accelerated scheme for the prediction of numerical shape function is developed, complemented by a physical residual-driven online correction strategy to tackle the degradation of the generalization at discontinuous 0/1 topological boundaries. Numerical validations demonstrate that the scheme drastically enhances computational efficiency while preserving global finite element analysis accuracy. Notably, computation time for a one-million degree-of-freedom (DOF) structure is reduced from 981.01 to 6.91 s. The developed approach is validated through three 3D full-scale numerical examples, including a cantilever beam, a cantilever plate, and an enclosed cylindrical energy harvester. Optimization results demonstrate that this scheme for electromechanical coupling problems is highly efficient and robust, effectively driving topology reconstruction to suppress local charge cancellation effects. Consequently, the final energy conversion rate is enhanced by up to 1.56 times over the initial configuration. Furthermore, comparisons confirm that these lattice structures yield higher absolute electrical energy output than conventional dense solid designs, which highlights their anticipated values in the applications in environmental energy harvesting.

papers.title: The AI-FinTech Entrepreneurial Ecosystem: Exploring How Intelligent Financial Technologies and Algorithmic Digital Visibility Transform Opportunity Recognition and Venture Growth. A Comparative Study of Pakistan and China
papers.venue: Journal of Business Insight and Innovation
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence and financial technology are increasingly intertwined with the digital platforms through which entrepreneurs discover opportunities, secure finance, reach customers, and scale ventures. This qualitative comparative study develops an integrated view of the AI-FinTech entrepreneurial ecosystem by examining how intelligent financial technologies and algorithmic digital visibility shape opportunity recognition and venture growth in Pakistan and China. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with 20 entrepreneurs, equally divided between the two countries, and the data were analyzed using reflexive thematic analysis. The analysis identifies six interrelated themes: AI-FinTech as an opportunity-sensing infrastructure; algorithmic visibility as a market-access mechanism; intelligent finance as a resource-orchestration capability; platform opacity and dependency; ecosystem asymmetry between Pakistan and China; and human judgment, trust, and governance as boundary conditions. The comparative findings indicate that AI-enabled financial intelligence creates value most effectively when entrepreneurs can convert data into action and when digital platforms provide stable routes to visibility, legitimacy, and customers. The study contributes an ecosystem-level explanation linking entrepreneurial alertness, dynamic capabilities, digital finance, and algorithmic visibility. papers.title: A Hybrid Large Language Model and Diffusion Framework for Rational Promoter Design
papers.abstract: High-performance promoters are essential tools for precisely regulating gene expression, yet their rational design within the vast combinatorial sequence space remains a major challenge. Here, we present a hybrid framework that integrates a large language model (LLM) with a diffusion model to enable data-driven and interpretable promoter design. The fine-tuned LLM predicts promoter strength with high accuracy and, through systematic sequence mutations, identifies biologically essential core regions. A diffusion model is then conditioned on these core regions to reconstruct non-core regions and generate complete promoter sequences. We experimentally validated this approach in Escherichia coli by high-throughput barcoded promoter activity sequencing: 7.78% of the designed promoters outperformed the benchmark promoter BBa_J23119, with the best variants reaching approximately 2.5-fold the expression level of BBa_J23119. By explicitly coupling interpretability with generative design, this strategy provides a practical framework for promoter design in E. coli and may be adaptable to other regulatory sequence engineering tasks.

papers.title: Risk-Aware Predictive Maintenance for Aero-Engines via CVaR-Guided Reinforcement Learning and LLM-Based Risk Abstraction
papers.abstract: A fundamental limitation of current predictive maintenance is the inability to transform prognostic uncertainty into actionable decisions, which often leads to either wasteful early interventions or catastrophic failures in aero-engines. To address this, we propose the Risk-Aware Predictive Maintenance (RAPM) framework consisting of four integrated components: a probabilistic stacked sparse autoencoder that extracts degradation features while providing distributional remaining useful life (RUL) predictions; a Monte Carlo Dropout module with Conditional Value at Risk (CVaR) that summarizes lower-tail predictive risk and produces a conservative RUL estimate for decision making; a locally deployed large language model (Qwen2.5-3B) that abstracts numerical uncertainty into discrete semantic risk levels, enabling interpretable reward shaping; and a Proximal Policy Optimization agent trained with curriculum learning to handle long-horizon sparse-reward maintenance optimization. On the NASA C-MAPSS FD001 benchmark, RAPM achieves a 96.0% optimal stopping rate with no late interventions or failure events compared with 90.2% for the strongest independent maintenance baseline. Under controlled substitution with LSTM-MCD, Transformer-MCD, CNN-MCD, and Deep Ensemble prognostic backbones, the same CVaR-LLM-PPO decision architecture maintains optimal stopping rates of 92.4–95.2% with no late interventions or failure events. Within the matched Rule-PPO ablation, CVaR increases the mean optimal stopping rate from 92.0% to 95.0% under unperturbed conditions, which is a gain of 3.0 percentage points. Under Gaussian sensor noise (σ=0.05), the gain reaches 9.0 percentage points, from 73.0% to 82.0%. These results demonstrate that the decision benefit of RAPM extends across independently trained prognostic models.

papers.title: Large Language Model-Driven Predictive Maintenance for Complex Industrial Processes: A Review and Future Research Directions
papers.abstract: With the rapid advancement of industrial intelligence, equipment predictive maintenance (PdM) has emerged as a critical enabler for intelligent operation and maintenance (O&M) systems. However, conventional machine learning-based PdM methods are inherently constrained by scarce labeled fault samples, weak cross-condition generalization, and a lack of advanced causal reasoning capabilities in complex industrial process environments. Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) and generative artificial intelligence (GAI) have created unprecedented opportunities to fundamentally overcome these persistent PdM limitations. This paper presents a comprehensive review and future perspective on LLM applications for PdM in industrial process systems and proposes a hierarchical “Capability-Domain-Method (CDM)” taxonomy to establish a unified analytical framework for this fast-growing research field. Based on a systematic analysis of the 103 core research papers published between 2016 and 2026, this work comprehensively summarizes the latest research on LLMs for predictive maintenance from three core technical dimensions: data augmentation, model adaptation, and knowledge reasoning and decision-making. Data augmentation methods generate high-fidelity fault samples and degradation patterns to mitigate industrial data scarcity and class imbalance. Model adaptation techniques empower general-purpose pre-trained LLMs to adapt to specific equipment and complex industrial environments. Knowledge reasoning and decision-making approaches integrate external industrial domain knowledge, autonomous reasoning mechanisms, and maintenance decision processes to improve the performance of fault diagnosis, root cause analysis, and maintenance decision-making. Furthermore, this paper discusses key challenges related to operational reliability, deep domain adaptation, unified evaluation standards, and unified deployment efficiency. Finally, future research directions are advised, including physics-informed large models, industrial domain-specific models, autonomous maintenance agents, and standardized open benchmarking platforms, to accelerate the paradigm shift in PdM from data-driven pattern to knowledge-driven and autonomous decision-making.
